promises.quote: The RCP has confirmed that the FPA will close in December, along with the PAMVR. The initial transfer of PAMVR data from the RCP to the GMC will begin on 31 October 2024. The GMC register will open on 13 December 2024, when regulation begins, but will continue to be voluntary for the first two years. The PAMVR will remain static, but searchable, until 31 March 2025 when it will be closed.
promises.summary: Close FPA and PAMVR, transfer data to GMC, open voluntary register

promises.quote: the GMC will become the regulator of PAs and anaesthesia associates (AAs) in December this year.
promises.summary: GMC to regulate PAs from December 2024

promises.quote: We are clear that statutory regulation is necessary for PAs and anaesthesia associates (AAs) and the UK and Scottish parliaments approved legislation in early 2024 which provides a legal duty for the GMC to regulate PAs and AAs from December 2024.
promises.summary: Statutory regulation of PAs and AAs begins December 2024

concerns.quote: There is no regulatory body with oversight of Physician Associates
concerns.hazard: lack of regulatory oversight of Physician Associates

concerns.quote: The Physicians Associate Managed Voluntary Register held by the Faculty of Physician Associates (FPA) is voluntary
concerns.hazard: voluntary register without mandatory employer verification

concerns.quote: There is no national framework as to how Physician Associates should be trained, supervised and deemed competent
concerns.hazard: absence of national training and supervision standards

concerns.quote: There remains limited understanding and awareness of the role of a Physician Associate both amongst medical colleagues, patients and their families
concerns.hazard: role confusion due to title and lack of uniform

concerns.quote: In June 2022 the Physicians Associate had been signed off as competent for the insertion of ascetic drains
concerns.hazard: inadequate competency assessment for ascitic drain insertion

promises.quote: We will ask the trust for the action they intend to take because of this Prevention of Future Deaths Report and monitor those actions as part of our ongoing monitoring and engagement with them.

promises.quote: NHS England has published a summary of existing guidance on the deployment of medical associate professions for NHS organisations. This guidance makes it clear that all staff should introduce themselves and their role clearly and be supported by their employer to do so.
promises.summary: Publish guidance on staff role introductions

promises.quote: RCEM issued a position statement in October 2024 regarding patients who may require a laparotomy [7]; this statement highlights that some patients are at greater risk of requiring surgery and part of this group includes the older person and those with cognitive impairment.
promises.summary: RCEM updated guidance on supervision of Physician Associates in emergency departments, requiring senior consultant review for high‑risk patients.

promises.quote: the Department notes that the report has been sent to a number of medical Royal Colleges and professional bodies relating to anaesthesia. We think these organisations are best placed to respond to points 6, 7 and 8 of your report which relate specifically to guidelines around anaesthesia therefore our response focuses on points 1 - 5 only.
promises.summary: Refer anaesthesia guideline concerns to medical Royal Colleges and professional bodies.

Lack of public understanding of the role of Physician Associate
The right of patients and family to seek a second opinion

Lack of 'Updated' National Guidelines for Rapid Sequence Induction (RSI) of Anaesthesia for emergency surgery

followups.summary: The legislation referenced was approved in early 2024 and sets a December 2024 start date for GMC regulation of PAs and AAs, but the provided sources do not confirm that statutory regulation was fully implemented by that date or that the promised legal duty was carried out.

sources.title: PA and AA Mandatory GMC Registration: 13 December 2026 | Sessional
sources.quote: From **13 December 2026**, practising as a PA or AA without GMC registration becomes a criminal offence under the Anaesthesia Associates and Physician Associates Order 2024
